comments.author: mitchellh
comments.text: These are Ghostty GUI release notes, but I want to take a moment to highlight the libghostty progress we've made since Ghostty 1.3. As a reminder, libghostty is the highly portable, embeddable library that provides core terminal emulation, render state, and more. I always felt that a free, high qualty, lightweight, reusable terminal emulation core would benefit the developer world more than any single GUI application. And that is playing out! It is and always was my true purpose with the Ghostty project (I said this in my first ever talk about Ghostty!). I've jokingly said many times that Ghostty GUI is just a glorified tech demo for libghostty. That's not fair though, because GUI is great and there are really talented people working on it. Since I started the project, Ghostty has always gotten people saying "I don't understand why you'd start a terminal emulator today." Well, the answer is libghostty. It's truly unique and its enabling something special (imo!). Highlights of libghostty since 6 months ago (none of the below was true 6 months ago): - Libghostty has nearly 100% coverage of all of Ghostty's core (and you can compile with flags to remove any of these features for size/safety): https://libghostty.tip.ghostty.org/ - Libghostty now builds and is tested (in CI) for: Apple (macOS, iOS, visionOS), Windows (MSVC and GNU), Linux, FreeBSD, Android, WebAssembly, and freestanding (i.e. direct on hardware with no OS). - Libghostty has bindings in pretty much every popular programming language: C, Zig, Go, Swift, Python, Rust, .NET, etc. - Libghostty's memory requirements have dramatically shrunk to enable the portability above. There's still work to do but a single empty terminal now takes 90% less memory. And at scale I've proven 10,000 active (input/output happening) terminals on a Linux server with 4 cores and 8 GB of RAM. - Libghostty powers all JetBrains IDE terminals, over 12.5 million active users. https://blog.jetbrains.com/platform/2026/10/jetbrains-termin... - Libghostty is the most popular core behind the wave of venture-backed "agentic" terminals and editors, such as Herdr, cmux, and many others. - Libghostty is being discussed and has been verbally accepted to replace the terminal core in Neovim: https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/39773 (work still to be done) - Libghostty powers a really popular and powerful terminal emulator for emacs (Ghostel): https://github.com/dakra/ghostel - Libghostty's speed is used by Antithesis to fuzz popular terminal programs and has directly led to hundreds of bug fixes sent upstream to programs such as tmux, btop, shells, and other terminal emulators. :) - And so much more: https://github.com/Uzaaft/awesome-libghostty Libghostty is really successfully turning into the tide that raises all boats. As it becomes more popular, Ghostty itself gets more performant and stable, and so does everyone else. It is also a vehicle for delivering modern terminal emulation to the widest source possible. I plan on tagging libghostty 1.0 in the next few months and declaring ABI stability at that point!

stories.title_en: Python's experimental JIT to be removed
stories.title_ja: Pythonの実験的JITが削除される

comments.author: adrian17
comments.text: Unfortunate. I've been following the work on it occasionally. On one hand, it seemed like JIT work was really progressing in high gear until SC requested a new PEP. Also unfortunate, as it seemed like part of the hope for the JIT was that it'd counter the performance penalty from free threading. On the other, it did feel (to me) like with all the fancy (and definitely cool) optimizations it got (automatic refcount operation removal, new type-based specializations, inplace math operations), the macrobenchmark benefits weren't _that_ exciting for a JIT. It definitely has potential for more, maybe with even fancier optimizations like unboxing ints, but the complexity just keeps going up. > It said that the PEP was "overly optimistic" about user-visible differences with the JIT enabled. The JIT is technically generated from the same source as the interpreter loop itself, so originally the differences were extremely unlikely, but I imagine the risk just kept going up as new JIT-only paths and optimizations were introduced. And politically, I feel like SC’s reasoning was just “this side project has landed in main branch almost by accident and has been stewing without oversight ever since, with no stabilization in sight”; and the latest PEP was probably still too vague, with a lot of “here’s more things we can add to the stew” - so I can understand if SC wasn’t satisfied.

comments.author: rich_sasha
comments.text: Here’s an idea instead (maybe it already exists). Allow a decorator for writing inline Cython. It solves, I think, 90% of the problem. On first run, or eagerly, compile the decorated functions. Basically, Cython is the JIT, and user enables it explicitly. This way I can easily write inlined functions with proper C speed, in a Python esque language. Reasons why I rarely use Cython without this: - unmodified Python code running in Cython is often faster, but not that much. 50% or so is my rule of thumb. - but the development style is very different for Cython and Python, adding a lot of impedance. Eg reloading doesn’t quite work, profiling is different, you need a build directory and a build step at deployment etc. - Cython proper is different enough and I’d argue unintuitive enough that if I have to have all these things in place, I might as well wrap my function in Rust. Such a decorator would give you a low friction way to make things faster when you need it, with scope for making it much faster via all the funny Cython, while keeping Python-esque semantics, in particular "development semantics". I think it would require some language modification since Cython was definitely a superset of Python; I think some of that syntax has been streamlined, but maybe still a strict superset.

stories.summary_ja:
**主な議論点**  
Pythonの実験的JIT（Just-In-Timeコンパイル）機能の削除について、パフォーマンス向上の期待と現実、および開発プロセス上の問題が議論された。JITは進歩していたが、マクロベンチマークで顕著な改善は見られず、複雑性が増す一方でメンテナンス負担も大きくなった。また、SC（Steering Council）がPEPの曖曼さや oversight不足を理由に削除を決定したことに対し、過程や政治的判断についての懸念が浮上。

**賛否両論**  
JITの潜力と技術的魅力を評価する声と、複雑性やメンテナンスコスト、PEP策定プロセスの問題を指摘する声が分かれた。一部のユーザーはJITの将来的な可能性（例: 整数アンボックス化）を期待しているが、他者は既存の代替手段（Cython, Numba, PyPyなど）の充実を理由に、JIT不要論を呈示。

**注目コメント**  
インラインCythonを可能にするデコレータの提案が特に注目された。開発者は、Cythonの高速性を維持しつつ、Pythonの開発体験を損なわない方法を求め、JITよりも低フリクションな代替案として Cythonの活用を提案。また、JavaScriptやRubyのJIT成功を背景に、Pythonのベース最適化水準や資金面での違いを比輸することで、JIT進展の課題を再評侰するコメントも掲載された。

stories.summary_ja:

comments.author: mrothroc
comments.text: This matches my own experience, pre-AI. As I've moved from IC to having a team over the years, more code was being written than I could possibly understand at the depth I would have if I'd written it myself. The skill I learned is exactly as you describe: understand the system. For me, this means "boxes and lines", the components and how they interact. I've encouraged developers on my team to make sequence diagrams part of their deliverable, because it helps both of us put the code in the context of the system. The boxes can be opaque because I know the boundaries and expected inputs and outputs. This tells me when I need to go in a box: is it sending a malformed message? I can trace that back into the code. I think that's the skill we have to cultivate now that coding agents produce far more than we can review line-by-line. The system view is the map, and the boundaries tell us where to go hunting inside the box.

comments.author: trjordan
comments.text: I like the analogy. It feels right. But I don't think it actually is, because it leans hard on the _feeling_ of failure, vs. the actual failure. The failure that actually matters here is product failure. Angry users. Security incidents. Downtime. Broken workflows. Stressed and uncomfortable developers have, historically, been a leading indicator of product failure. Software is complex and when devs can't handle the breadth of ownership + the depth of expertise at the same time, it means bad work that leads to product failure. It's not clear that agents fail in the same way, or that our collective intuition about how and when to trust agents is sufficiently developed to predict product failure in the same way. As anecdata: I know a bunch of growth-SaaS/last-batch-of-IPO companies where the devs are all stressed, the feature ship rate is up, and incidents are down. All at the same time. So yes, quick learners and just-in-time depth is important, but so is intuition about where discomfort is going to produce true failure. The discomfort isn't a feeling to throw away, simply trusting that you'll learn everything in time. Ownership requires holding a model of the system in your head and proactively steering where you dive.

comments.author: Peteragain
comments.text: It's rambling, but highlights a point. The big picture IMHO is that news as we ingest it is like history. History is viewed through a lens of the present and its concerns. News is viewed through the same lens, filtered by the concerns of, not journalists, but what journalists think we are concerned with. Real journalists (IE investigative) don't present "facts", but interpret "facts" against a world view. Good journalists state how they do that. Just to put the cat out and see what happens, Michael Moore is definitive at this, irrespective of whether or not you agree with his world view, at least you know what his world view is. I've just had a piece of Reform UK advertising through the mailbox, and it is printed in the format and style of news. Nice trick. I guess that is what 70 million GBP of overseas funding buys you.

stories.summary_ja:
**主な議論点**: ニュースは「事実」ではなく、現在の視点や読者の関心でフィルタリングされた解釈である。歴史と同様、「物事の真実」よりも「語り方」が重要である。特に、ジャーナリスト自身の立場が明示されていない断片的なニュースが問題視されている。

**賛否両論**: 一部の人は、ニューズが中立的事実伝達を装う問題を指摘し批判。一方で、Michael Mooreのように立場を明確にしたジャーナリストを評価する声もある。また、政治宣伝をニュースの体裁に偽装する事例（例: Reform UK選告）に対する批判も集まった。

**注目コメント**: 「Real journalists state how they do that」——優れたジャーナリズムは、自らの解釈に基づいていることを隠さず、透明に立場を示すべきであるという主張に多くの共感が集まった。

stories.summary_ja:
・主な議論点  
コミュニティでは、PHP2Shellの実際の悪用について意見が分かれた。一方では、一般的な攻撃や実際のエクスプロイトがほとんど観測されていないとの見解があり、一方で一部のハニーポットや研究者による成功した悪用例が報告されている。特に、Adel Karimi氏のハニーポットでのエクスプロイトや、Trail of Bitsが開発したとされる「ユニバーサルエクスプロイト」、Bleeping Computerの報告などが注目された。

・賛否両論  
肯定的な意見では、悪用実績やハニーポットデータ、信頼性の高いセキュリティ企業の警告を根拠に、即刻のパッチ適用と監査が求求されるべきだとの立場がある。一方、懐疑的な意見では、広範な実悪用は確認されておらず、過度な緊張感は不要ではないかという見方もあり、現時点では防御策を整えつつ状況を注視すべきだとの意見も示された。

・注目コメント  
Adel Karimi氏のハニーポットでのエクスプロイト成功がCISAによるKEVリスト掲載に影響を与えた可能性が指摘されており、実際の攻撃データが政府のセキュリティポリシーに反映されている事例が興味深い。また、Fil-CへのPHP移植によってエクスプロイトをDoS攻撃に変換できる可能性についても技術的検証が進んでいる。

If I had a copy of myself I would tell him "do the thing", but agents say "do the thing like this and this, it must be such and such, use X and put it together that way". The subagent is just as intelligent but now it's constrained, sometimes as you start developing something you discover some things are better organized in a different way etc. So it spends much time figuring out how to deliver exactly what was asked even if it's not optimal because that's the task. stories.summary_ja:
**主な議論点**  
AIツールの導入により、優秀なエンジニアの生産性は飛躍的に向上している一方で、そうでないエンジニアの問題は悪化している。特に、AIに頼りすぎて本質的な設計判断やコードレビューを怠る傾向が指摘されている。また、要求仕様が曖昧な状態でAIエージェントを追加すると、速くて間違った解答が出されるだけであるが、それによって逆に正しい要求を導き出す新しいアプローチも可能になっているという意見もある。

**賛否両論**  
AIの活用によって生産性が向上するメリットについては広く認められるが、エンジニアの能力差がさらに拡大しているという懸念もある。また、AIエージェントは細部まで指示を決めがちで柔軟性に欠けるため、最適な解決策を見出すことが難しいとの批判もある。一方で、従来の逐次作業モデルが終わりつつあるとして、複数タスクの並行処理 here是とする意見もあるが、それには高度なコンテキスト管理能力が必要となる。

**注目コメント**  
「AIエージェントは自分自身に指示を出すのが下手」という指摘が興味深い。エージェント同士の通信やタスク管理において、過剰な制約や不適切な指示が非効率性を招くことが指摘されており、人間のように柔軟な指示出しや判断が求められていることが強調されている。

comments.author: mandevil
comments.text: For a while (2018-2022) it was hot to buy up software companies that dominated a single niche and jack up prices. The bet was that since software is such a 0-1 business that they would have great moats and have strong pricing power. My father-in-law is blind and used to use JAWS until it got bought up by a private equity firm (Vispero) which tried to dominate the software accessibility market and jacked up the prices to annual subscriptions. He's a electrical engineer so he was comfortable switching to free software NVDA, but a lot of people paid up. Now with LLM's that business model is in shambles and the finance side of it is less attractive with interest rates so high. I suspect that this is actually driving the software engineer hiring slow-down, because these companies were actually doing most of the employing of software engineers, much more than the big tech companies.

comments.author: chollida1
comments.text: One interesting knock on from the hyperscaler growth we've seen is that the Mag7 have issued so much debt that they are crowding out other companies who would otherwise have no trouble issuing debt. The private equity and private credit crowd is one of these groups that are currently running into this issue. There is no way a growing company($15M to $500M in yearly sales is the sweet spot for these private credit companies) can compete with Google on debt terms so they have to raise their rates to compete suddenly, not because of all rates rising but strictly because we've just seen a huge debt issuance from some very solid credit companies. We haven't seen a shock like this in 20+ years I've followed the credit market where a small group of companies issue so much high quality debt in such a short period of time, note there is also a lot of less high quality debt issued in this same time:) So much has been issued that credit funds have run out of appetite to acquire Lowe middle market debt at their current spreads. This is just the way markets work so no one is crying in the casino but it is a big shock to the credit markets. heck there was concern that the US government may have trouble issuing 5-10Y debt at rates they are used to because of the amount of GOOG, META,etc debt that is available at better terms. Its a wrinkle to the markets that no one really predicted as a knock on effect of AI's growth. This is all the back drop for BDC(Business Development Companies) and other private credit issuers who normally loan money for 5-7 year terms. Those cheap 2021 loans to these small private companies are now coming due into this market with the additional head wind that the largest single sector that issued debt was venture backed software companies, who now face the head winds of the macro factors described above and the additional factor of AI commoditizing alot of hte software that these companies are building. Private credit and equity are going to have a rough couple of years. Things to watch out for are lack of IPO's and exist from venture/PE backed companies and a proliferation of continuation funds that kick the can down the road. On the plus side, its a great time to be a credit trader, but not necessarily a credit issuer:)

comments.author: woeirua
comments.text: I have not seen spec first development work well in real world environments at all. The problem is that you typically don't know what you don't know upfront for most product based decisions. Going back and forth in the spec to fix problems is a huge mistake, it just leads to contradictory sets of requirements for the agent. What does work well is using AI to generate a quick and dirty prototype ala vibecoding, and then using that as a basis to regenerate the final code. Some might say it's still spec driven development, but the spec is a working prototype.

stories.summary_ja:
**主な議論点**  
仕様ファースト開発が実環境でうまく機能しない懸念が中心。最初に仕様を完全に定義することは難しく、後から修正すると矛盾した要件が生じる。AIによるプロトタイプ生成が有効だとの意見もあり、プロトタイプを最終コードのベースにする「vibe coding」的アプローチが提案された。

**賛否両論**  
一部は仕様ファーストのリスクを指摘。仕様が曖昧であれば、エージェントが生成するコードも不安定になるとの見解。一方で、仕様を「実行可能なプロトタイプ」として再定義する方法も評価されている。

**注目コメント**  
「仕様がエージェントによって編集可能でなければ、コードと同じく非決定的になる」 — 仕様の柔軟性と実行可能性の重要性を指摘するコメントが話題を集めた。

stories.summary_ja:
**主な議論点**  
Hacker Newsユーザーたちは、AnthropicがClaude Codeのプラン選択画面でデータ使用について明確な約束をしたにもかか64648れ、実際の利用において不透明なデータの取り扱いに懸念を抱いている。特に、フィードバックを送信する際のポップアップや評価ボタンのクリックが訓練データとして利用される可能性について議論が巻き起こしている。

stories.title_ja: ソフトウェアは悪くなっているのかもしれないが、かつてはもっとひどかった

comments.author: i_c_b
comments.text: It's interesting that he brings up Diablo 2 and Diablo 3 (and Quake for that matter), though, because I think it really foregrounds why these discussions are so fraught. I worked in early AAA in the late 90s, and it's true that games were often quite rough around the edges. But they were also often biting off WAY more than they could chew, inventing genres and innovating like crazy, often in messy ways that didn't always work. But that meant players were often also routinely and genuinely surprised by the experiences they encountered in even big budget games. He lists a bunch of quality of life and balance issues that were fixed in Diablo 3 compared to Diablo 2... but, well, Diablo 2 was obviously _important_ in ways that Diablo 3 wasn't. It's a much greater game. And lurking in the background is the hard fact that often the progress with software (certainly game software) entailed turning to much better software engineering standards, using much better external libraries or game engines with much larger teams, and relying on much more process to capture and filter all those rough edges... and along the way, you've built a much, much larger team with a much larger burn rate, and so all those experiments and innovations become much more dangerous and need to be corralled and controlled and mostly stifled, and as the cost of all this to build skyrockets your entire game design _has_ to focus on your business model and your microtransaction story and your live services first and foremost, because you've boxed yourself into a corner where that cash flow issue is the central fact of your game / software design. (I experienced this evolution first hand in the FPS space) All of which is to say, I think there are multiple different axes at play here for evaluation, and it's probably fair to say that software _undefinably_ was much worse in the past along some of them... but not all of them. And there are probably deep tensions and tradeoffs between some of those axes. I think this entirely discussion really is muddied, though, too, by the fact that hardware got radically better over this entire arc as well, and so many programming techniques in the past that made software more brittle or crash prone hinged on memory and computation optimizations techniques that really had nothing to do with the software culture of then or now. It was just a response to the realities of the hardware.

comments.author: xmddmx
comments.text: ^F Latency - no hits found. Latency is one metric by which computing has gotten noticeably worse over the years. Daily, I encounter multiple situations in which I take some action (click a button, type text in a text field, etc.) and the response is visibly delayed - from several hundred to several thousand milliseconds. This used to happen only on websites, but lately is also happening on apps installed on my computer. The cause? My theory is that everything is now some sort of monstrosity of React or similar web app, running inside a browser process, and possibly even that local apps are sending data round-trip up to the mothership for tracking, surveillance, synchronization, etc. And the UX is terrible - often while this is happening, stale data is showing, or there is no visual indication a process is underway.

comments.author: quacked
comments.text: All of these are examples of the physical performance of software or hardware limitations at the time. I find that software's reliability has increased a thousandfold in my lifetime, but its actual controllability/feel/UI-UX has been rapidly declining for about a decade.

comments.author: brookst
comments.text: “Software is degrading for obvious reasons” is just painfully lazy. Where are the metrics of degradation? Where are the claims of specific reasons, and the evidence of causality? If the complaint is vibe coding makes bad software, I largely believe it, but I absolutely believe that vibe arguing makes tissue paper arguments. “Everyone knows” and “it’s obvious” are flimsy things to rest arguments on. I’m writing dramatically better software for all the reasons this post says obviously make worse software. Testing has gotten much easier, and bug fixing has gotten much easier. I looked at a pre-AI project I did a couple of years ago: test to code LOC was 0.15:1. The projects I work on now are around 1.3:1. The old project had no accessibility considered at all, the new ones are nicely done aria and beyond. Old project is stuck on old libraries because upgrading is a major pain. New projects take new libraries (after cooldown) no matter the effort. So I’m left thinking that perhaps some people, too lazy to use the new powers of new tools, churn out the same or worse quality code/essays. But I am seeing a lot of very high quality software that simply wouldn’t have been possible before, and I believe the same could be done with essays by leveraging these tools to research and find real data beyond “it’s obvious”. But that does take a lot more work.

comments.author: Pannoniae
comments.text: IMO it's a bit more nuanced than what the author portrays it as. Broadly, software used to be much worse on the micro-level but better on the macro-level i.e. architecture. Since it was much harder to make stuff, you really had to architect it well or otherwise it would simply fall apart. For example in assembler you need discipline in your calling conventions, layout and so on, otherwise it just corrupted, you needed to follow sensible naming conventions otherwise it degenerated into unreadable label spaghetti and so on. Nowadays it's the other way around, the micro level is so much better due to libraries, code reuse, LLMs and better languages/tools, you can use highly sophisticated data structures and functions at your fingertips. In exchange, you can afford to skimp on architecture because computers are fast anyway, and the programming languages don't let you make a huge mess. (Most don't have unstructured goto/jumps, can't corrupt memory accidentally, etc.) However, this has the cost of making larger programs a nightmare to maintain and systems suffering from a "death of thousand cuts" i.e. on the micro level all is well but when you look at the entire system it's a sprawling unreliable mess. This is where rewrites often happen ;)

stories.summary_ja:
・主な議論点  
ソフトウェアの品質劣化について、過去と現在のトレードオフがテーマに浮かび上がった。特にゲームやアプリの開発プロセスが複雑化・大規模化し、革新性や冒険性が抑制されているとの意見が多く、歴史的に重要な作品（例えば Diablo 2）は革新的だったが現代版（Diablo 3）は安全策に走っているとの指摘がされた。また、ハードウェアの進化により過去の最適化が文化や設計に影響を与えていたことも言及された。  

・賛否両論  
一方で、開発ツールやテスト環境の向上により、ソフトウェアの信頼性やアクセシビリティが向上しているとの肯定的な意見もある。特に AI や LLM の活用により開発効率が飆高に上がっているとの見方もあり、質の低下はある程度個人の責務によるとする意見も出た。しかし、UI/UX の反応速度や設計の直感性は反面、近年悪化しているという批判も多い。  

・注目コメント  
「ソフトウェアは過去に比べマクロ（アーキテクチャ）では優れているが、マイクロ（コード品質）では劣化している」とのコメントが注目された。過去のアセンブラ時代には厳密な設計が求められていたが、現在は言語やライブラリの進化により短所が緩和され、全体としては複雑化・保守性低下という新たな問題が生じているという論点が興味深い。

comments.author: fallat
comments.text: The standard library is lacking some really nice conveniences. I'm working on correcting this and teaching Forth as a "grassroots" language for people who want to go back to the joy of programming as an art. The 100rabbits folks have already done a lot of work around proliferating that idea but I want to work outside of the Uxn machine that they use. stories.summary_ja:
・主な議論点  
コメントでは、Gforth 1.0のリリースを受けて、Forth言語の教育的価値や魅力についての議論が展開された。特に、標準ライブラリの貧弱さが課題として挙げられ、これを改善するための取組が進められていることが強調された。また、Forthは「 Grassroots」アプローチで、プログラミングの楽しみを取り戻すための言語として位置づけられ、AIの台頭によってプログラミングの面白みが失われることに対する抵抗感も表現された。さらに、Gforthが依然としてネイティブOS実行ファイルの生成能力を欠いているという技術的不足も指摘された。

・賛否両論  
Forthの教育的価値や芸術性を高める動きには肯定的な声が多く、「プログラミングのjoy」を求める層に対応していると評価する意見が多かった。一方で、実用的な面での不足（標準ライブラリの不足やネイティブコンパイルの欠如）に対する批判もあり、Gforthの現代的な使いやすさに疑問の声も投げ掛けられていた。

・注目コメント  
「Forth will continue to exercise our brains and work through logic and data flow problems - skills we can bring to guiding agents for the day job.」  
このコメントは、Forthの学習が単なるプログラミングの復習ではなく、AI時代の思考訓練でもあると指摘しており、実務と教養の橋渡しとしての価値を象徴的に表現している。

stories.summary_ja:
・主な議論点
このアルゴリズムは、ピクセルあたり約0.5バイトのメモリ使用量と、経路を記録する点が特徴です。スタックがピクセル数に限定されているため、ヒープの一部として実装できると指摘され、概念的に理解しやすいという評価得到了。

・賛否両論
肯定的な意見として、実際の開発で困った経験を持つ人が「このスタックレス版に変換する」と実用的な利点を強調しました。一方で、union-find（連結成分解析）を別途の選択肢として挙げるユーザーもおり、 O(N)のメモリと計算時間は同じだが、異なるアプローチが存在することに注意が向けられました。

・注目コメント
「1ピクセルの隙間」に対する扱いについての疑問が挙げられました。アルゴリズムはその隙間に入れるが、戻るための仕組み（バックトラッキング）が apparent にないため、算法の理解が不十分かもしれないという懸念が示され、詳細な説明の必要性が示唆されました。
